title: Phone Case Designer with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a phone case designer using Three.js. The scene features a 3D phone case model and a loaded WaterBottle.glb asset as a decorative reference object. Follow these specifications exactly:

## Scene Setup
- Use Three.js with OrbitControls and GLTFLoader from CDN.
- Create a perspective camera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (5, 10, 5) with intensity 1.0.
- Set renderer background color to #1a1a2e.
- Add a grid helper (size 10, divisions 10) on the ground plane.

## Phone Case Model
- Create a phone case using Three.js geometry: a RoundedBox or a BoxGeometry(0.8, 1.6, 0.1) with MeshStandardMaterial. Position it at (0, 1.5, 0).
- The phone case material should start with color #3498db (blue) and metalness 0.3, roughness 0.7.

## WaterBottle.glb Asset
- Load 'WaterBottle.glb' using GLTFLoader and place it at position (2, 0, 0) with scale (5, 5, 5). This serves as a reference/companion product.

## Color Picker UI
- Add a DOM panel (div) with id='controls-panel' positioned at top-left with background rgba(0,0,0,0.8), padding 15px.
- Add 5 color buttons with class='color-btn' and data-color attributes: #3498db (Blue), #e74c3c (Red), #2ecc71 (Green), #f39c12 (Orange), #9b59b6 (Purple). Each button should be 40x40px circles.
- Clicking a color button changes the phone case material color to that color.

## Physics Debug Overlay
- Add a toggle button with id='debug-toggle' labeled 'Toggle Debug' in the controls panel.
- When debug mode is ON, display a semi-transparent overlay div with id='debug-overlay' showing:
  - Camera position (x, y, z) rounded to 2 decimals
  - Phone case world position
  - Current case color hex
  - Frame count
  - A wireframe mode is enabled on the phone case (set wireframe=true on material)
- When debug mode is OFF, hide the overlay and disable wireframe.

## Texture Pattern Toggle
- Add a button with id='pattern-toggle' labeled 'Toggle Pattern' in the controls panel.
- Clicking it cycles through 3 states: 'solid' (no map), 'stripes' (create a canvas texture with horizontal stripes), 'dots' (create a canvas texture with polka dots).
- The pattern is applied as the map property of the phone case material.

## Keyboard Interaction
- Press 'R' key to reset the phone case rotation to (0, 0, 0).
- Press 'Space' to spin the phone case (add a continuous Y rotation of 0.02 per frame). Press Space again to stop.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields:
  - caseColor: current hex color string of the phone case (e.g., '#3498db')
  - debugMode: boolean, whether debug overlay is visible
  - pattern: string, one of 'solid', 'stripes', 'dots'
  - spinning: boolean, whether auto-rotation is active
  - caseRotationY: number, current Y rotation of phone case in radians
  - bottleLoaded: boolean, true once WaterBottle.glb is loaded
  - frameCount: integer, incremented each animation frame
  - wireframe: boolean, current wireframe state of phone case material

## Animation Loop
- Increment frameCount each frame.
- If spinning is true, add 0.02 to phone case Y rotation each frame.
- Update debug overlay text each frame if debug mode is on.
- Update caseRotationY in __3D_STATE__ each frame.
physics_constraints: No physics simulation required. Rotation values must remain finite (no NaN/Infinity). Frame count must monotonically increase. Color values must be valid hex strings.
